newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian bourse launches index after delay.
newsitem.headline: Latvian bourse launches index after delay.

text.p: The Latvian stock exchange finally launched its own index on Wednesday, which was delayed by two months due to technical problems.
The Latvian market has been open for more than two years. From a handful of companies, it now includes around 40.
The index is a capitalisation index of nine shares, five from the leading official list and four of the most active stocks from the secondary list.
The index is calculated from a base of 100 on April 2 1996. It rose one percent to 379.98 on Wednesday.

"According to comparative data of the European Federation of Stock Exchanges, the Latvian bourse registered the biggest growth in eastern Europe in 1996," bourse president Uldis Cerps told a news conference.
"Investors who invested a year and a half ago have seen a return on equity of 300 percent and 150 percent for those who invested a year ago," he added.

Although the market has developed well, foreign investors often complain that the companies listed are too small and illiquid and are waiting for the listing of large, infrastructure companies before getting seriously involved.
But Cerps noted that the bourse's market capitalisation rose to 157.43 million lats against 29 million lats in June 1996.
He said the index would add more shares as the big privatised infrastructure companies hit the market.
"I think the number of companies in the index will grow to reach 12 or 13 by the year end," Cerps said.
"It is important to have the index in place as the market will enjoy a faster development at the end of summer and autumn," Cerps said.
"It will allow portfolio investors to calculate their net assets and performance relative to the index," he added.
